# ytx — YouTube → JSON (metadata and transcript)

A .NET global tool that extracts YouTube video metadata and transcripts as JSON.

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ",
  "videoId": "dQw4w9WgXcQ",
  "title": "Video title",
  "channel": "Channel name",
  "channelId": "UCuAXFkgsw1L7xaCfnd5JJOw",
  "uploadDate": "2009-10-25",
  "durationSeconds": 212,
  "viewCount": 1700000000,
  "keywords": ["keyword"],
  "description": "Video description...",
  "captionStatus": "ok",
  "captionLanguage": "en",
  "captionLanguageName": "English",
  "captionIsAutoGenerated": false,
  "captionError": null,
  "transcriptRaw": "Full transcript as one string...",
  "transcript": "## Intro\n\n- [00:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&t=3s) First line\n- [00:07](...) Next line",
  "segments": null,
  "chapters": [
    { "start": 0, "end": 43, "title": "Intro" },
    { "start": 43, "end": 212, "title": "Chorus" }
  ]
}
```

## Features

- 🎯 **Single JSON output** — Clean, structured data for easy parsing
- 🌍 **Captions-aware** — Prefers human-written captions in your language, reports which track it used
- 📝 **Markdown transcript** — Human-readable format with timestamped links, split into sections by chapter
- 📑 **Chapters** — Read from the video description, using YouTube's own rules
- 🚀 **Cross-platform** — Works on macOS, Windows, Linux (.NET 8/9/10)
- ⚡ **Fast & lightweight** — No dependencies beyond .NET and YoutubeExplode

## Quick Start

### Install from NuGet

```bash
dotnet tool install -g solrevdev.ytx
```

### Usage

```bash
# Existing/primary usage: the URL does not require a switch
ytx "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"

# Via JSON input
echo '{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"}' | ytx

# Save to file
ytx "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ" > video-data.json

# Show command help or the installed package version
ytx --help
ytx --version
```

The positional URL and piped JSON forms are the original interfaces and remain supported. `--url` is available when an explicit option is more convenient.

- Piped JSON uses only its `url` key; other keys are ignored. Pass options such as `--language` as arguments.
- A URL given as an argument wins, and piped input is then not read.
- Put `--` before a video ID that starts with `-`, for example `ytx -- -AbCdEfGhIj`.

### Options

```text
-u, --url <value>         Specify the YouTube URL or video ID explicitly
-l, --language <value>    Prefer captions matching a language name or code
                          (default: English). Falls back to English, then
                          any track, with a warning on stderr
    --metadata-only       Skip caption retrieval and return metadata only
-f, --format <format>     json (default), or only the transcript as md, txt,
                          srt or vtt
    --segments            Add a segments array of {start, end, text} to the
                          JSON, with times in seconds
    --list-languages      List the video's caption tracks as JSON and exit
    --proxy <url>         Send requests through this proxy, such as
                          http://host:8080 or socks5://host:1080. Without it,
                          HTTPS_PROXY and the system proxy are used
    --timeout <seconds>   Give up after this many seconds (default: none)
-c, --compact             Write compact JSON instead of indented JSON
-h, -?, --help            Show help and exit
-v, --version             Show the ytx version and exit
```

Examples:

```bash
# A bare 11-character YouTube video ID is also accepted
ytx dQw4w9WgXcQ

# Prefer French captions; falls back to English with a warning on stderr
ytx --language fr "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"

# See which caption tracks a video has
ytx --list-languages dQw4w9WgXcQ

# Write subtitles, or plain text with one caption per line
ytx --format srt dQw4w9WgXcQ > video.srt
ytx --format txt dQw4w9WgXcQ

# Add timed segments for agents and tools
ytx --segments dQw4w9WgXcQ

# Work from a server or CI runner through a proxy
ytx --proxy http://user:pass@proxy.example:8080 dQw4w9WgXcQ

# Retrieve only the metadata and emit one-line JSON
ytx --metadata-only --compact "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"
```

### Upgrade

```bash
dotnet tool update -g solrevdev.ytx
```

## Output Format

Every document has the same keys in the same order. Fields that YouTube does not provide are `null`, never missing.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `url` | Canonical watch URL, whatever form of URL or ID was passed in |
| `videoId` | 11-character video ID |
| `title` | Video title |
| `channel` | Channel name |
| `channelId` | Channel ID |
| `uploadDate` | Upload date as `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `durationSeconds` | Length in whole seconds, or `null` for a live stream |
| `viewCount` | View count |
| `keywords` | Video tags (may be empty) |
| `description` | Full video description |
| `captionStatus` | `ok`, `none` (the video has no captions), `skipped` (`--metadata-only`), `blocked` (YouTube refused the request) or `error` |
| `captionLanguage` | Language code of the track used, such as `en` or `pt-BR` |
| `captionLanguageName` | Language name of the track used |
| `captionIsAutoGenerated` | `true` for YouTube's automatic captions, `false` for human-written ones |
| `captionError` | Error message when `captionStatus` is `blocked` or `error` |
| `transcriptRaw` | All caption text as a single normalized string |
| `transcript` | Markdown list with `[HH:MM:SS](link) text` format |
| `segments` | With `--segments`, an array of `{start, end, text}` with times in seconds to the millisecond; otherwise `null` |
| `chapters` | Chapters from the description as `{start, end, title}` in seconds; `end` is `null` for the last chapter of a live stream. `[]` when the video has none. Also filled with `--metadata-only` |

**Chapters.** ytx reads the timestamped lines that creators put in the description, such as `0:00 Intro` or `(03:12) - Setup`, and applies YouTube's rules: the list starts at `0:00`, has at least three entries in increasing order, each chapter lasts at least 10 seconds, and the lines form one block. A list that breaks a rule gives `[]`, so tracklists and stray timestamps are not mistaken for chapters. YouTube's auto-generated "key moments" are not included. When a video has chapters, `transcript` and `--format md` start each chapter with a `## Title` heading.

With `--format md|txt|srt|vtt`, only the transcript is written, with no JSON. If there is no transcript, stdout is empty and stderr says why. The exit codes are the same as for JSON.

`--list-languages` writes `{"videoId": "...", "tracks": [{"code": "en", "name": "English", "isAutoGenerated": false}, ...]}`. Pass a `code` or `name` from it to `--language`.

When `captionStatus` is not `ok`, the caption fields are `null` and both transcript fields are empty. Check `captionStatus` rather than the transcript text.

## Development

### Local Build & Test

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/solrevdev/solrevdev.ytx.git
cd solrevdev.ytx

# Restore dependencies
dotnet restore src/Ytx

# Build
dotnet build src/Ytx -c Release

# Run the unit tests (on .NET 8, 9 and 10; add -f net8.0 to use one runtime)
dotnet test tests/Ytx.Tests -c Release

# Test locally (choose an installed target framework)
dotnet run --project src/Ytx --framework net10.0 -- "YOUR_YOUTUBE_URL"
dotnet run --project src/Ytx --framework net10.0 -- --help

# Pack for local installation
dotnet pack src/Ytx -c Release
dotnet tool install -g solrevdev.ytx --add-source ./nupkg
```

### Project Structure

```
├── src/Ytx/Program.cs              # CLI and extraction implementation
├── src/Ytx/Ytx.csproj              # Package and target-framework metadata
├── tests/Ytx.Tests/                 # CLI parsing and formatting unit tests
├── .github/workflows/publish.yml   # Validation and release automation
├── .github/workflows/codeql.yml    # CodeQL analysis
├── assets/icon.svg                  # Package icon source (icon.png is rendered from it)
├── CHANGELOG.md                     # Release history
├── docs/investigations/             # Write-ups of reviews and investigations
└── README.md                        # User and maintainer documentation
```

## CI/CD

This project uses `.github/workflows/publish.yml` for validation and publishing:

- Pull requests that change the source, tests, or workflow restore, build, test, and pack the project without publishing.
- A push to `master` that changes the source or publishing workflow automatically performs a **patch** release.
- A manual workflow run can instead select a patch, minor, or major release.
- The publishing job reads the current `<Version>` from `Ytx.csproj`, calculates the next version, builds and tests it, packs that version, and publishes it to NuGet with a short-lived key from NuGet Trusted Publishing.
- Only after NuGet accepts the package does the job commit the new `<Version>` to `master`, create the matching `vX.Y.Z` tag, and create a GitHub Release.
- Publishing is serialized, checks that `master` has not moved, and uses `--skip-duplicate` plus release-state checks so a failed run can be retried safely.

Do not manually edit `<Version>` for an ordinary patch release. Merge or push the source change to `master` and let the workflow bump it exactly once. A version should only be edited deliberately when changing the release process itself.

### Manual Release

Go to Actions → "Publish NuGet (ytx)" → "Run workflow" and choose your version bump type.

### Maintainer release checklist

1. Test, build, and pack locally with `dotnet test tests/Ytx.Tests -c Release`, `dotnet build src/Ytx -c Release`, and `dotnet pack src/Ytx -c Release`.
2. Open a pull request for validation, or push an approved change to `master` for an automatic patch release.
3. Watch the "Publish NuGet (ytx)" workflow. A successful run publishes NuGet first, then pushes the version commit and tag.
4. Confirm the new version on NuGet or with `dotnet tool update -g solrevdev.ytx`, then run `ytx --version`.

The GitHub Actions workflow uses NuGet Trusted Publishing and does not need a stored API key. If publication fails, fix the cause and rerun the same workflow; do not manually bump the project version before retrying.

## Exit Codes

- `0` — Success, including a video with no captions (`captionStatus` is `none`)
- `1` — The video could not be retrieved, or another unexpected error
- `2` — Usage error (missing or invalid URL)
- `3` — Metadata was written to stdout, but captions were blocked or failed (`captionStatus` is `blocked` or `error`)
- `130` — Cancelled with Ctrl+C

## Known Limitations

- Private, age-restricted, or region-blocked videos may not provide transcripts
- Videos with disabled captions return `captionStatus: "none"`
- YouTube blocks many cloud and datacenter IP addresses, which shows up as `captionStatus: "blocked"` or exit code `1`. Use `--proxy` or `HTTPS_PROXY` with a residential proxy
- Markdown timestamps are rounded down to whole seconds; `segments`, SRT and WebVTT keep milliseconds
- Large transcripts are not truncated (full output provided)
